name: baseline-variance
title: Baseline variance
description: Variance of a P6 project against its baseline or another project: finish variance, slip causes, the activities that moved most, logic changes and earned value at the data date. Use when the user asks to compare a project with its baseline or with another version.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: baseline
args.description: Project ID of the baseline or project to compare with (empty: the project baseline)

template:
Baseline variance of project {project}: finish variance, slip causes, the activities that moved most, logic changes and earned value at the data date, against the baseline {baseline} (the project baseline when it is empty). Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): dates, baseline used, finish variance.
2. act = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{baseline}", section="activities", min_variance_days=1, limit=20): activity summary, slip causes, largest finish variances. If this call returns an error, keep its message as act.error (its other fields are null).
3. rel = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{baseline}", section="relationships", limit=20): relationships added, removed or with another lag. If this call returns an error, keep its message as rel.error (its other fields are null).
4. pc = p6_progress_curve(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): earned value in units at the data date. If this call returns an error, keep its message as pc.error (its other fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

# Baseline variance of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}.

[if: bl_used]
Compared with the baseline {bl_used} ({bl_source}), baseline data date {bl_data_date}. Activities are matched by Activity ID.
[end if]

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and variances are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: bl_used]
No baseline: {project} has no project baseline and none was given. Assign a project baseline in P6 or run this skill again with the Project ID of a baseline. The variance cannot be reported.
[end if]

## Project finish

- Scheduled finish {finish}; baseline finish {bl_finish}; finish variance {fv_cd} cd, {fv_wd} wd proj (positive = later).
- Must finish by {must_finish}: the scheduled finish is {mf_cd} cd, {mf_wd} wd proj after it (negative = before).

## Activities

[if: act_error]
The activity comparison failed: {act_error}
[end if]

- Matched {matched}; only in the project (added) {added}; only in the baseline (removed) {removed}.
- Finishing later {later}, earlier {earlier}, same finish {same_finish}. Later ones: average {later_avg_cd} cd, largest {later_max_cd} cd; earliest {earlier_max_cd} cd.
- Status changed {status_changed}; original duration changed {dur_changed}; name changed {name_changed}; no slip cause (calendar or date missing) {slip_unknown}.

Slip causes of the matched activities (late_start: the start moved; longer_duration: the start-to-finish span grew; on_time: same finish within 5 minutes of work):

[table: causes]

### Largest finish variances

Start and finish are actual, else early dates of the last F9. Start var + duration delta = finish var, in working days of each activity's calendar.

[table: moved]

## Logic changes

[if: rel_error]
The relationship comparison failed: {rel_error}
[end if]

- Relationships matched {rel_matched}; added {rel_added}; removed {rel_removed}; lag changed {rel_lag_changed}.

[table: links]

## Earned value at the data date (units, h)

[if: pc_error]
The progress curve failed: {pc_error}
[end if]

- Baseline planned {bl_planned}, earned {earned}, actual {actual}.
- Schedule variance (earned - baseline planned) {ev_variance}; SPI (earned / baseline planned) {spi}; actual / baseline planned {spi_actual}.

Units are labor and nonlabor assignments, spread linearly between their dates (an approximation of P6's spread); earned = budget x activity % complete.

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- sum.baseline.used is null (no project baseline and no baseline given): write the title, the data date line
  and the "No baseline" block of reference/report.md, then stop. Never compare with another project you chose.
- A baseline was given and a call says it is not found: repeat the message and stop.

## Errors of optional calls

- act, rel or pc returned an error: keep the report, write its "failed" block with the message; the slots
  and tables of that call are n/a or left out. Never rebuild them from another call.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. sum.schedule_state.data_date = act.schedule_state.data_date = rel.schedule_state.data_date =
   pc.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. sum.baseline.used = act.other = rel.other = pc.baseline.project (same baseline).
3. sum.dates.scheduled_finish = act.projects.scd_end_date.project (same project finish).
4. sum.baseline.finish = act.projects.scd_end_date.other (same baseline finish).
5. sum.baseline.spi_units = pc.to_date.spi (same SPI).
6. act.summary.relationships.matched = rel.summary.relationships.matched.

A failed call is not checked. If a group differs, the database changed between the calls: run the calls
again once. If it still differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- Finish variance in cd and wd proj comes from sum.baseline, never from subtracting two dates.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (causes 10, moved 20, links 20).
  A table whose call has more pages (next_offset not null) ends with its line "Showing the first
  <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers copied from that call.
- Every activity is written "Activity ID - name", in the links table too.
- The warning block is kept only when schedule_state.stale is true.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Baseline variance

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): dates, baseline used, finish variance.
2. act = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{baseline}", section="activities", min_variance_days=1, limit=20): activity summary, slip causes, largest finish variances. If this call returns an error, keep its message as act.error (its other fields are null).
3. rel = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{baseline}", section="relationships", limit=20): relationships added, removed or with another lag. If this call returns an error, keep its message as rel.error (its other fields are null).
4. pc = p6_progress_curve(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): earned value in units at the data date. If this call returns an error, keep its message as pc.error (its other fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {baseline}: Project ID of the baseline or project to compare with (empty: the project baseline), as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- wd proj: working days of the project calendar
- cd: calendar days
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- h: hours
- count: a count

## Table causes

Matched activities per slip cause.

Rows: act.summary.activities.slip_causes, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 causes are shown.
No rows: write 'No matched activity.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Slip cause | _key |  | text | n/a |  |
| Activities | _value | count | int | n/a |  |

## Table moved

Added and removed first, then matched ones moved by 1 cd or more, largest absolute variance first.
